title: Chapter 104: Give Me One Minute
html:
The apartment was immaculate and thickly carpeted. Heavy cloth padded every table and counter edge. A plate of fruit sat on the coffee table, but there were no knives, forks, or other sharp objects.

“Doctor Gao, please come in.” A well-groomed woman in her forties, dressed in white, welcomed Doctor Gao and Chen Ge inside.

“Has Wang Xin’s condition improved?”

“I’ve given her the prescribed sleeping pills and antidepressants, but they haven’t helped.” The woman smiled weakly. “Her condition is unchanged, while the side effects keep getting worse—retching, chills, trembling hands. At lunch she couldn’t hold her chopsticks and spilled food everywhere. Doctor Gao, can Wang Xin still recover?”

“Believe me, she will get better.”

The woman nodded, then noticed Chen Ge behind him. “And this is?”

“My name is Chen Ge.” Chen Ge did not want to waste time. “Can I please meet your daughter?”

“This…” The woman turned to Doctor Gao to ask for his opinion.

“I’ll be with him.” At Doctor Gao’s nod, the woman reluctantly stepped aside. “She’s in her bedroom. After one spoonful at lunch, she began screaming.”

She approached a door and knocked softly for some time. When no answer came, she turned the knob and opened it a crack. With a silent sigh, she stepped back.

“Let’s go in.” Doctor Gao turned to Chen Ge. “Do not provoke her. Before you try anything, discuss it with me.”

“All right,” Chen Ge promised as they entered. The bedroom carpet was even thicker. Every cupboard and table edge had been rounded smooth, and security mesh covered the windows. There was nothing sharp in sight. Two thick mattresses lay together in place of a bed. Everything was white, with no personal belongings anywhere.

Doctor Gao moved aside, revealing the person Chen Ge had come to find. A slender young woman lay on the mattress. Her round-collared white shirt hung from her thin frame, and her skin was so pale it seemed translucent. She looked as though one sudden movement might break her.

Noticing the visitors, she slowly sat up. Chen Ge had expected agitation or violence. Instead, she appeared perfectly lucid, only withdrawn.

Doctor Gao crouched beside the mattress so their eyes were level. “Wang Xin, does your head still hurt?” he asked gently.

She shook her head, glanced at Chen Ge, then lowered her gaze.

“Have you been sleeping?” This question provoked a much stronger reaction. She grabbed her hair, and when her hand opened, black strands clung between her fingers. She had torn them out by the roots.

“Still no sleep?” Doctor Gao rose, his brow deeply furrowed. “Neither medication helped?”

“Doctor Gao, may I speak to her?”

“Her condition is stable for the moment. Go ahead.” Chen Ge crouched as Doctor Gao had. Wang Xin probably assumed he was another doctor and showed little resistance. She merely tugged down her sleeves to conceal the red welts left by her own frantic scratching.

She seemed as fragile as a paper kite held to life by a single thread. One mistake, and the storm would tear her away into darkness.

“Wang Xin.” Chen Ge pulled out the ballpoint pen from his pocket. “Your friend wants to talk to you, so I brought her with me.”

Wang Xin glanced at the pen without recognition. Perhaps she wanted to smile at what sounded like a joke, but even that was beyond her.

Doctor Gao and the woman listening from the doorway exchanged confused looks. Undeterred by Wang Xin’s silence, Chen Ge took a sheet of white paper from the desk and laid it on the mattress. He poised the pen above it, ready to begin the Pen Spirit game.

With his back to Doctor Gao and his face toward Wang Xin, Chen Ge silently mouthed the invocation. “Pen Spirit, Pen Spirit, you are my…”

His moving lips gradually captured Wang Xin’s attention. She turned fully toward him and read the words. Recognition struck. Her arms flailed, and she recoiled against the wall as a terrible memory resurfaced.

“What are you doing?!” The woman dashed into the room to stop Chen Ge alongside Doctor Gao.

“I’m helping her confront the source of her condition.” Chen Ge shielded the pen. “No one knows what happened to Wang Xin, but that secret is what made her ill. Give me one minute—that’s all I need.”

He remained beside the mattress, pen firm in his hand. At first, he had wanted only to complete the Pen Spirit’s mission. After seeing Wang Xin’s torment, he genuinely wanted to help her.

“Let’s give him a chance.” After a long standoff, Doctor Gao chose to trust him. “Wang Xin has never reacted this way during our sessions. It may be a positive sign.”

Doctor Gao persuaded the woman to allow three minutes. They retreated to the doorway while Chen Ge closed the curtains and the door.

“Wang Xin, your friend has been trying to reach you.” He placed the pen above the paper again and continued to chant. “Pen Spirit, Pen Spirit, you are my spirit from my previous life, and I am your spirit in this life…”

As he continued the chant, fear overtook the girl in the corner. The nightmare that had haunted her for years rose again. Cruel though it felt, Chen Ge forced himself to continue. Soon the pen moved on its own, tracing elegant handwriting utterly unlike his.

“Wang Xin, I never imagined a foolish prank would leave such a deep wound. You must hate me, don’t you?”

Wang Xin stared at the familiar handwriting, stunned beyond thought.

“My death was not your fault. When I saw you coming with another friend, I only meant to frighten you. I never expected the rope to tighten or the chair to slip.

“You did nothing wrong; it was a silly prank gone very wrong.

“I’m so sorry, Wang Xin. I won’t ask you to forgive me, but I hope you can let go of these terrible memories and live the best life you can—for all of us.”
